description: An infrared orthophoto map displaying CORINE Land Cover (CLC) classifications in a mountainous environment, illustrating the spatial distribution of glaciers and surrounding land cover types. The base imagery, consistent with an infrared orthophoto, renders "CLC: Glaciers and perpetual snow" as prominent magenta (pink) areas. These areas are delineated by yellow outlines, as are other CLC classes. "CLC: Bare rock" is shown in darker blue tones, "CLC: Sparsely vegetated areas" appears in greenish-blue, and "CLC: Moors and heathland" is represented by greenish-brownish areas towards the bottom of the map. The map visually differentiates these land cover categories, showing boundaries between permanent ice/snow, exposed rock, and various sparse vegetation types, typical of high-altitude regions such as Kebnekaise, Sweden, as referenced in the document context.
